In image2, the black corner mark of the input paper is still at the lower left corner; after passing through machine S, the corner mark is still at the lower left corner, and at the same time there is an upright plum blossom symbol added on the paper, indicating that S only prints the plum blossom in a fixed direction and does not rotate the paper. In the target images of image3 and image4, the black corner mark is located at the upper right corner, and the plum blossom symbol has rotated 90 degrees clockwise relative to the upright plum blossom in image2. Reasoning: The black corner mark of the starting paper is at the lower left corner. To make the corner mark finally reach the upper right corner, it needs to be rotated 90 degrees clockwise twice, so among the three machine steps there must be two R's and one S. The plum blossom printed by S is upright at first; the target plum blossom has rotated 90 degrees clockwise, indicating that after S prints, it still has to pass through one more R rotation. Since there are two R's in total, and one R is needed after S, then the other R must be before S. Therefore the order is R, S, R.

Read from image3/image4 that the target has the corner mark at the upper-right and the club turned 90 degrees clockwise from the upright club. Starting with the blank marked square at lower-left, the final upper-right corner mark requires two clockwise rotations total, so among the three slots there must be two R operations and one S operation. Since the club in the target is rotated 90 degrees clockwise, it must be printed before exactly one final R. Therefore the sequence is R, then S, then R.

method.method_draft: Backward inverse route: Start from the target picture in image3/image4. The target club is not upright; it appears rotated 90 degrees clockwise, and the black corner mark is at the upper-right. If the last machine were S, the club would have just been printed upright, so the last machine must be R. Undo this last R by rotating the target 90 degrees counterclockwise: the corner mark becomes upper-left and the club becomes upright. Since this upright club must have appeared immediately before the final rotation, the middle machine is S. Removing the print leaves a blank square with the corner mark at upper-left. Compare this with the original blank square, whose mark is lower-left; image1 shows that one R changes lower-left to upper-left. Thus the first machine is R, giving RSR.
